questions.q: Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
A firewall blocks all inbound traffic except services that are explicitly allowed. Which principle is this?
Why is Telnet unsafe for managing a router?
options: It sends credentials in plain text
It blocks SSH on the same port

questions.q: What does network segmentation mainly achieve?
options: Limits how far an attacker can move after a breach

questions.q: Staff at a Pune branch see a new Wi-Fi network with a name like the company's near the lobby. Many devices joined it. What is the likely threat?
options: An evil-twin access point capturing traffic

questions.q: A server's connection table fills with half-open TCP connections from many random IPs. What attack is this?
options: A SYN flood denial of service

questions.q: Why is TLS inspection at a corporate proxy considered a trade-off?
options: It removes the need for endpoint security
Visibility gained, but end-to-end trust and privacy suffer

questions.q: An internal server sends DNS queries with long random-looking subdomains to one external domain every minute. What do you suspect?
options: DNS tunnelling for command-and-control or data theft

questions.q: Which control best stops a compromised laptop on the LAN from reaching the database subnet directly?
options: Internal firewall rules allowing only the app servers

questions.q: A login form builds its database query by joining user input into the query string. What vulnerability is this?
What is the right fix for SQL injection in application code?
What does the HttpOnly flag on a cookie do?
options: Sends the cookie only over plain HTTP
Stops page scripts from reading the cookie
Makes the cookie expire on logout

questions.q: A comment box shows users' input on the page without encoding, and an attacker posts a script. What is this?
On an order page, changing /orders/1045 to /orders/1046 shows another customer's address and UPI ID. What is the flaw?
What does an anti-CSRF token protect against?
options: Data read straight from the database
Forged requests from another site riding the user's session

questions.q: A file upload accepts any file type and stores it in the web root. What is the biggest risk?
options: Files take too much disk space
A script gets uploaded and run by the server

questions.q: A feature fetches a user-supplied URL to show a link preview. A tester enters http://169.254.169.254/. What risk are they checking?
options: SSRF reaching the cloud metadata service
DNS rebinding of the user's browser
Brute force of the admin page

questions.q: Why is a Content Security Policy useful even when output is already encoded?
options: It blocks SQL injection at the database
It is a second layer limiting which scripts can run

questions.q: A JWT-based API accepts tokens whose header says "alg": "none". What is the impact?
options: Anyone can forge tokens without a signature

questions.q: What is the safest way to store user passwords?
options: AES encryption with a shared key
A slow salted hash like bcrypt or Argon2

questions.q: Which is an example of multi-factor authentication?
options: Password plus an authenticator app code

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean?
options: Each user gets only the access their work needs
All staff get admin rights to save time
Access is removed only when someone leaves
One shared account is used per team

questions.q: A finance employee in Hyderabad moved to the sales team last month but can still open payroll files. Which control failed?
Why is an SMS OTP weaker than an authenticator app or hardware key?
options: SIM swap and interception can expose the code

questions.q: A cloud service account key was pushed to a public GitHub repository an hour ago. What should you do first?
options: Delete the commit and move on
Revoke and rotate the key immediately
Make the repo private and wait
Email the team to be careful

questions.q: Why are standing admin rights riskier than just-in-time admin access?
options: Admins cannot use MFA with standing rights
A stolen admin account stays useful to attackers at all times

questions.q: Logs show hundreds of accounts each failing one login from varied IPs within minutes, using common passwords. What attack is this and the best control?
options: Password spraying; enforce MFA and ban weak passwords
Brute force on one account; lock that account

questions.q: What does federated SSO (SAML or OIDC) mainly give a company that uses 30 SaaS apps?
options: Central login control and quick offboarding
No need for authorisation checks in apps

questions.q: An email that looks like it is from the CEO asks an accountant to urgently send ₹4 lakh to a new vendor. What is this?
What is ransomware?
options: Malware that encrypts data and demands payment

questions.q: A user clicked a suspicious link and typed their office password into the page. What should they do first?
options: Wait to see if anything happens
Delete the email and forget it
Report it and change the password at once

questions.q: In the incident response lifecycle, which phase comes right before eradication?
A server shows signs of compromise and the admin wants to reboot it immediately. Why might you object?
options: Reboots are banned during office hours
A reboot can wipe memory evidence needed for investigation
Rebooting spreads malware to the network

questions.q: Under CERT-In's 2022 directions, within how long must many types of cyber incidents be reported?
Which pattern in Windows logs suggests lateral movement?
options: One account remotely logging into many servers quickly
A user changing the desktop wallpaper
Print jobs sent late at night

questions.q: Ransomware encrypted file servers at a Chennai hospital. Backups exist but were joined to the same domain. What is the key step before restoring?
options: Pay the ransom to get the key fast
Confirm backups are clean and the attacker's access is removed

questions.q: Why keep a chain of custody for forensic disk images?
options: So evidence is accepted as untampered in legal action
To share images freely with vendors

questions.q: EDR flags powershell.exe started by winword.exe with an encoded command line. What is the best immediate action?
options: Isolate the host and collect the process tree
Ignore it since PowerShell is a Microsoft tool
Reset only the domain admin password

questions.q: What does a SIEM mainly do?
options: Collects and correlates logs to raise alerts

questions.q: Why should security patches be applied promptly?
options: Attackers quickly exploit publicly known flaws
Old versions stop working the next day
Patches remove the need for backups

questions.q: A vulnerability scan returns 400 findings. How should you prioritise them?
options: In alphabetical order of host name
By exploitability and asset exposure, not only CVSS
Lowest severity first since they are quick

questions.q: Under India's DPDP Act 2023, what is an organisation that decides how personal data is processed called?
A SOC receives 2,000 alerts a day and analysts ignore most of them. What is the best fix?
options: Tune rules using false-positive rates and add context
Hire more analysts and keep all rules

questions.q: Why should at least one backup copy be offline or immutable?
options: Offline storage is cheaper per GB
So ransomware with admin access cannot encrypt or delete it

task.title: Investigate a suspicious web server log
task.brief: You are on shift and get this web server log extract from an Indian online shop (see material). In 20-30 minutes, write a short incident note. Cover: 1) each attack you can see, which IP did it, and whether it looks successful (with the log line that shows it); 2) what data was likely exposed and how serious this is; 3) the first actions you would take in the next hour, in order; 4) the fixes needed so it does not happen again, including any reporting duty in India. Plain sentences or bullet points are fine.
task.material:
nginx access log extract, shop.example.in (times IST, 14 Nov 2026). Format: IP - [time] "request" status bytes

103.21.44.17 - [02:10:03] "GET /products?id=12 HTTP/1.1" 200 5120
103.21.44.17 - [02:10:09] "GET /products?id=12' HTTP/1.1" 500 312
103.21.44.17 - [02:10:15] "GET /products?id=12%20OR%201=1-- HTTP/1.1" 200 98211
103.21.44.17 - [02:10:31] "GET /products?id=12%20UNION%20SELECT%20username,password_hash%20FROM%20admins-- HTTP/1.1" 200 5388
49.36.8.201  - [02:11:02] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2210
103.21.44.17 - [02:12:40] "GET /download?file=../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1" 200 1874
185.220.9.4  - [02:14:00] "POST /admin/login HTTP/1.1" 401 210
185.220.9.4  - [02:14:01] "POST /admin/login HTTP/1.1" 401 210
185.220.9.4  - [02:14:01] "POST /admin/login HTTP/1.1" 401 210
   ... 1,412 more identical 401 lines from 185.220.9.4 until 02:31:55 ...
185.220.9.4  - [02:32:07] "POST /admin/login HTTP/1.1" 302 0
185.220.9.4  - [02:32:09] "GET /admin/dashboard HTTP/1.1" 200 7740
185.220.9.4  - [02:33:45] "GET /admin/export?table=customers&format=csv HTTP/1.1" 200 48211904
49.36.8.201  - [02:35:10] "GET /cart HTTP/1.1" 200 3301

Context: the customers table holds names, phone numbers, delivery addresses and UPI IDs.
There is no MFA on /admin/login. The app runs on one VM; the database is on the same VM.
key_points: SQL injection from 103.21.44.17; the OR 1=1 response size jump and UNION query returning 200 suggest success, admin hashes likely exposed
Path traversal on /download returned 200 with /etc/passwd; likely successful
Brute force or credential stuffing from 185.220.9.4 ending in a 302 success and admin dashboard access
Large customer CSV export (~48 MB) means personal data including UPI IDs was likely stolen
Contain: block the IPs, disable or reset admin accounts and sessions, take the export/download features offline, preserve logs and a VM snapshot
Fix: parameterised queries, file path allow-listing, MFA, rate limiting and lockout, least-privilege DB user, WAF/monitoring alerts
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours and handle DPDP obligations (notify the Data Protection Board and affected customers)

rubric.label: Finds the attacks
rubric.guide: 0 = misses most attacks, 3 = finds two of the three with some evidence, 5 = all three found with the right lines and success judged correctly

rubric.label: Judges the impact
rubric.guide: 0 = no view on impact, 3 = says data may be exposed, 5 = links the export to customer personal data and rates severity sensibly

rubric.label: Sound first actions
rubric.guide: 0 = no plan or harmful steps (e.g. wipe the VM), 3 = reasonable but unordered, 5 = contain, preserve evidence and reset access in a sensible order

rubric.label: Fixes and reporting
rubric.guide: 0 = none, 3 = generic advice, 5 = specific fixes for each flaw plus CERT-In and DPDP reporting
